legend: The only difference between the easy version and the hard version of the problem is the constraints on n%%ZSMJ0%%, k%%ZSMJ1%%, and ai%%ZSMJ2%%.

It's the year 2125, and e-archaeologists have uncovered remnants of what they believe was known as the "troll face". They believe that the troll face was represented by a non-degenerate k%%ZSMJ3%%-sided polygon that could be inscribed in a circle.

So far, the e-archaeologists have discovered n%%ZSMJ4%% line segments, each of which has a length ai%%ZSMJ5%%. Now, the e-archaeologists are wondering: how many k%%ZSMJ6%%-size subsets of their n%%ZSMJ7%% line segments could be used to create a troll face? Output your answer in mod 109+7%%ZSMJ8%%.
Consider all line segments to be unique, even if 2 have the same length.
input: The first line of input contains 2 integers, n%%ZSMJ9%% and k%%ZSMJ10%% (3≤k≤n≤100%%ZSMJ11%%) — the number of line segments and the number of sides in a troll face, respectively.
The second line of input contains n%%ZSMJ12%% integers, a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ13%% (1≤ai≤104%%ZSMJ14%%) — the lengths of the n%%ZSMJ15%% line segments.
output: Output a single integer in mod 109+7%%ZSMJ16%%, the number of k%%ZSMJ17%%-size subsets that could be used to create a troll face.
